To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SH2 domain-mediated PLC gamma activation is not required for Ca2+ release to initiate the fertilization reaction in mouse eggs.

the SH2 domains of phospholipases Cgamma 1 and Cgamma 2, which inhibit activation of these phospholipases by the PDGF-receptor, do not inhibit Ca(2+) release at fertilization when introduced into mouse eggs in large excess over the concentrations endogenous proteins.
SH2 domain-mediated PLCgamma activation does not initiate Ca2+ signaling at fertilization of the mouse egg.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that initiate the release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores at fertilization in the mouse egg.
the role of phospholipids and protein kinase C in the regulation of Ca(2+)-dependent exocytosis in sea urchin eggs and the role of protein kinase C in fertilization.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie Ca2+ release and the initiation of the cell cycle at fertilization of animal eggs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SH2 domain-mediated PLC activation is not required to trigger fertilization-induced Ca2+ release, but that it may be important for other aspects of fertilization.

SH2 domain-mediated PLCgamma activation is not required to induce Ca2+ release during fertilization in mouse oocytes, but the SH2 domains of both PLCgamma1 and 2 inhibit PLCgamma activation in mouse oocytes and may therefore be important in regulating PLCgamma activity in these cells.
SH2 domain mediated activation of PLCgamma is not required for initiation of Ca2(2+) release at fertilization, but it may play an important role at later stages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SH2 domain-mediated PLCgamma activation is not necessary for Ca(2+)(i) release at fertilization but that other PLCgamma-activating pathways are likely to exist.

PLCgamma does not appear to be the enzyme that initiates Ca2+ release during fertilization in mouse, and possibly other mammalian eggs.
